title: the-builds-tool-calls-are-evidence-about-the-chart
owner: CC owns the code and the proofs. Akien owns two bounds already given and not CC's to widen: that the finding goes back into 'our mechanisms' (the declared -2- route, not a new private channel), and that a mid-build SECOND CHART RUN is not what this is (he dropped that the same day and ranked it least important
intention: Observe the tool calls a /sail voyage actually makes, and turn the ones that contradict a chart berth into findings routed back to the chain that authored the claim.
why: AKIEN, 2026-08-14, collapsing /chart into /sail: it 'runs in sail, gets feedback about tool calls that happen inside the build. and we add that feedback into our mechanisms.' THE LIVED SYMPTOM, and it is a builder's, felt every voyage: the chart chain tells you what exists, what is absent, and where the edges are — and then the build finds out. survey says the holding is not there; you open it in step 2 and it is. constrain draws a bound; the real work sits one directory outside it. orient names an address; the code lives elsewhere. Today every one of those is absorbed silently by the builder, who adjusts and keeps going, and the chain that was WRONG never hears about it. The next voyage over the same territory re-derives the same correction from scratch — which is Law 1's defect stated exactly. What makes this a build rather than a wish is that the findings are ALREADY SPECIFIED and have simply had nowhere to go: skills/sail's own falsifier names 'a bound from the constrain berth silently widened' and 'a holding rebuilt in parallel' as reds, and both are tool-call-visible. The gap is not knowing what a finding is; it is that nothing looks.
traces_to: Akien's segment drawing, 2026-08-14 — machine -> inspector -1-> findings -> gate -> output -2-> feedback to [the upstream creative entity]. Here the BUILD is the machine and the chart chain is the upstream creative entity, which is what makes this a segment and not a new idea.
Law 1 — the resolver is spent on the novel. A correction the builder makes in their head and does not deposit is re-derived next voyage; that is the defect, not a nuisance.
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. A chart berth's claims are hypotheses until a build runs against them; the tool calls ARE the measurement and are currently thrown away.
Law 10 — nothing in the system is immeasurable. The calls are JSON on disk in the same file two shipped programs already parse, so 'we have not built it yet' is the true state.
skills/sail/intention+why.json feedback route -> skills/chart, declared 2026-08-14 ahead of this producer.
cairn/tools/feedback — the tool that owns the -2- edge and the shape of a declared route.

falsifier.proves_green: SHAPE BEFORE CODE, and the shape question is what keeps this at THINKME: WHAT COUNTS AS A CONTRADICTION. A voyage makes hundreds of tool calls and nearly all of them are ordinary; an observer that reports every call not foreseen by survey is a firehose, and a firehose is how a feedback channel gets muted in week one. The three candidates CC can see, offered as candidates: (1) NAMED CLAIMS ONLY — a finding only where a berth made a checkable assertion (survey's absences, constrain's out-list, orient's address), which is narrow, cheap, and provably non-noisy because the claim set is finite and already written; (2) CLAIM SET PLUS SHAPE — (1) plus structural surprises like a write outside every charted path; (3) EVERYTHING NOT FORESEEN, which is the firehose and is named here to be refused explicitly rather than drifted into. CC would build (1) and grow it against real findings (build-minimal), but the choice is a design call and the ticket does not pre-empt it.
falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) the observer reports a call as a contradiction when no berth made a claim about it — that is the firehose, and one such report is enough because it is the failure that silences the channel; (2) a finding is produced but names no berth field it falsifies, i.e. a complaint rather than a measurement; (3) the reader greps the raw JSONL instead of parsing records, which reports False on real content because the file stores \n and \uXXXX escaped (this failure has bitten twice in this corpus and is now a known tooth); (4) the observer becomes a second CHART RUN by another name — re-deriving orientation mid-build is exactly what Akien dropped, and this is the drift with the shortest path; (5) findings are written somewhere other than the declared -2- route, which would be a private channel and 'add that feedback into our mechanisms' says otherwise.
falsifier.horizon: Not urgent and the reason is measurable, not a feeling: nothing delivers along the -2- edge for ANY producer yet (cairn/tools/feedback edge (a)), so a finding produced today would sit exactly where a finding not produced today sits. It becomes urgent when the deliverer lands, and it should be built BEFORE the deliverer only if the deliverer needs a real finding to grow against — which it probably does, and that ordering argument is the one real reason to move this early.

questions.a: THIS IS NOT THE SECOND CHART RUN. Akien designed one and dropped it the same day — the condition was 'how much had changed for that component since the first chart run was taken', and he called the whole idea the least important part (skills/sail filed edge (d)). A second run RE-ANSWERS the chain's questions mid-build; this OBSERVES and reports and answers nothing. Anything that starts re-orienting mid-build has become the dropped thing and is red by falsifier (4).

THIS IS NOT THE BUILD INSPECTOR. cairn/machines/build_inspector judges a build against the berths that charted it and routes its findings to ticketing — it asks 'is this build good enough'. This asks the mirror question, 'was the CHART right', and routes to the chain. Same voyage, opposite direction, different address. A reader who merges them will delete one of the two edges.

THE FINDING'S SUBJECT IS ITS ADDRESS, and that is the open question one level up. A widened bound is constrain's, a rebuilt holding is survey's, a wrong address is orient's — and today the route names skills/chart, the whole chain, because one segment declares one address. Ticket a-segments-outbound-edge-carries-one-address holds that question and this is its cleanest case, because here the subject is READ OFF THE FINDING rather than inferred. This ticket must not settle it in passing.

CORRECTED BY AKIEN THE SAME DAY IT WAS CAST, and the correction is large enough that a reader must meet it before the text above. TWO THINGS THIS TICKET GOT WRONG. (1) THE WHY IS NOT TOKEN SPEND. It was cast carrying the economics of the 2026-07-19 pre-build-packet paper — pay for the preamble once, starve the model down to the novel core. Akien: 'The goal is not to reduce token spend for you. you are cached.' The real why is the STAIRCASE: the preamble migrates off Claude onto Hex (the M1 Studio, hex.local), Hex deposits graph tree nodes, and the pass answers the next one itself. Claude keeps doing the BUILDS, which is what makes Claude the ground truth rather than the thing being optimized: 'the system learns from you.' (2) THE SIGNAL IS A SCORE, NOT A SET OF PER-CLAIM FALSIFICATIONS. This ticket's gates argue about what counts as a contradiction and how to avoid a firehose. Akien: 'you can score the quality of the information downward just by doing more tool calls before the build is done.' The measurement is CALL VOLUME between the packet and done — more calls means the packet was worse — and it is one number, already emitted, needing no claim-anchoring and no adjudication of what counts. That collapses the firehose problem rather than solving it: there is nothing to filter because nothing is being classified. The per-claim shape is not deleted from the record because it may still be the right SECOND thing (a score says a packet was bad, not which field was), but it is no longer the first thing, and it is not what this ticket builds.

watchme: none, because there is nothing yet to drift and the honest instrument does not exist to hold it. What a watch would guard — that the observer keeps finding real falsifications rather than degrading to noise — is a question about the observer's OUTPUT QUALITY, and the first build cannot know the answer's shape (see gates: the whole risk here is a firehose, not a silence). A watch cast now would be a threshold invented before a single finding exists, which is the hand-set constant in a gate that learns-its-gates exists to refuse. Recast at PROVEME, when there are real findings to set it from.
dependencies: MEASURED 2026-08-14, so the reader is not a guess: the tool calls are in the session transcript at ~/.claude/projects/-home-akien-dev-src-cairn/*.jsonl, and TWO SHIPPED PROGRAMS ALREADY PARSE THAT EXACT GLOB — bin/cmd/turnscan (DEFAULT_CORPUS at :206) and cairn/machines/ruling/corpus.py (:49). Neither needs a new dependency beyond json and pathlib.

AND THE SHARPEST FACT ABOUT THOSE TWO: both DISCARD the tool calls. turnscan keeps end_turn messages; corpus.py skips any record carrying tool_use_id (:74). So the data has been passing under two readers' hands all along, deliberately filtered out by both. This ticket is not a new instrument class; it is the third reader of a file already read twice.
The chart berths are on disk and already claim-keyed, so 'which berth made this claim' is a lookup and not an inference: `python3 -m skills.chart.live chain <ticket-id>`.
NOT a dependency: the ticketing machine (cairn/tools/feedback edge (g)). This route targets skills/chart, which exists.

chart_notes.orient: The data is at ~/.claude/projects/-home-akien-dev-src-cairn/*.jsonl — the same glob turnscan and ruling/corpus.py already open, and both filter tool calls out (corpus.py:74 skips tool_use_id records; turnscan keeps end_turn messages). The claims to check against are the berths, reachable by command rather than by eyeballing: `python3 -m skills.chart.live chain <ticket-id>`. The berth fields that make checkable assertions are survey's absences and holdings, constrain's out-list, and orient's address.
chart_notes.constrain: OUT: a second chart run, any mid-build re-orientation, any new channel that is not the declared -2- route, and any priority or urgency field on a finding (the feedback tool's route is an address and nothing else — 'we're leaving room for those, we're not building or ticketing those now'). Also OUT: deciding which chart LEG a finding belongs to as a routing key — that is a-segments-outbound-edge-carries-one-address and it is Akien's.
chart_notes.validate: The tooth a hollow build fails: take a real voyage transcript and a real chart chain where survey listed a holding as ABSENT and the build opened it anyway, and require the finding to name survey's absence field and the call that falsified it. A hollow build passes by listing tool calls, or by reporting 'unexpected file access' with no berth field attached — falsifier (2) is exactly that tooth. Second tooth, and it has bitten this corpus twice: substring-match the raw JSONL instead of parsing records and a real path reports absent, because the file stores its content escaped. Parse; never grep.

filed_edges: If (1) is built — findings only where a berth made a checkable claim — then the SET of checkable claims becomes load-bearing, and it is currently implicit in each stage's schema rather than declared anywhere. That would want naming in the chart grammar rather than inferred from which fields happen to look assertive.

The same observation would serve a question nobody has asked yet: which berth fields NEVER get falsified. A field that no build has ever contradicted is either very good or never checked, and the two are distinguishable only by counting. Not this build.
